If every path through the body of a loop ends in `break`, `return`, or `throw`, the loop never gets to a second pass. Usually a condition is missing around the exit, or `continue` was meant.

## Examples

Reported. Only the first result is ever looked at:

{/* bad */}
```js
function firstError(results) {
  for (const result of results) {
    if (result.ok) {
      return null;
    } else {
      return result.error;
    }
  }
}
```

Not reported:

{/* good */}
```js
function firstError(results) {
  for (const result of results) {
    if (!result.ok) {
      return result.error;
    }
  }
  return null;
}
```

## Options

| Option | Default | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ignore` | `[]` | Kinds of loops to skip: `"WhileStatement"`, `"DoWhileStatement"`, `"ForStatement"`, `"ForInStatement"`, `"ForOfStatement"`. |

A `for...of` loop that returns at once is a short way to get the first item of an iterable. By default it is reported:

{/* bad */}
```js
function first(items) {
  for (const item of items) {
    return item;
  }
}
```

{/* good {"options": [{"ignore": ["ForOfStatement"]}]} */}
```js
function first(items) {
  for (const item of items) {
    return item;
  }
}
```
